clue.text: Russian conspirator's crimes involved with debt

indicators.note: crimes tangled up with debt: the two words' letters are mixed together into a new order

explanation.surface: A Russian plotter's offences are bound up with money he owes.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'conspirator' stands for 'is', a link joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Decembrists were Russian army officers who plotted an uprising against the Tsar in December 1825.

clue.text: Foppish fellow openly resisted when speaking

indicators.note: when speaking means the words are said aloud, so letters that sound the same are wanted

parts.note: Dan is a man's name, standing for any fellow; defied means openly resisted

explanation.surface: A dandyish man resisted in the open when he talked.
explanation.definitionFit: Dandified describes someone dressed like a dandy, overly fussy about clothes, as a fop is.

clue.text: What solicitors do in place of trials?

definitions.meaning: those who solicit, in the sense of seeking someone's affection, woo them

explanation.surface: A query about what lawyers get up to in a courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitors' suggests lawyers, but here they are suitors who woo; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To court is to woo or seek favour, and a court is also the building where trials take place.

clue.text: Girl Friday reportedly composed old opus about autumn

indicators.note: reportedly means as said aloud, so letters that sound the same are wanted

parts.note: made means composed or created
fall is the American word for autumn
an opus is a work

explanation.surface: A female assistant is said to have written an ancient piece about the autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: MAID spoken is the same as made, composed.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl Friday is a female general helper, like a servant who does every kind of household task.

clue.text: First-class workers in extremely robust clothing

indicators.note: the other pieces go inside the extremes of robust
extremely points to the outside letters of robust

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written AI in crosswords
men are workers, as in a firm's men

explanation.surface: Top-rate labourers dressed in very sturdy garments.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an old literary word for clothes or garments.

clue.text: Dairy product in list carried by close relative

indicators.note: the close relative carries the list inside him

parts.note: a son is a close relative
to list is to lean over, as a ship tilts

explanation.surface: A milk product shown on a menu brought by a family member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'list' is not a written catalogue but leaning, as a ship does.
explanation.definitionFit: Stilton is a strong English blue cheese, a dairy product.

clue.text: Peacekeepers infiltrating old army? Something fishy here

indicators.note: the peacekeepers work their way inside the old army, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, the British volunteer reserve, now renamed the Army Reserve
UN, the United Nations, which sends peacekeeping forces

explanation.surface: UN troops slipping into a veteran force seems suspicious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something fishy' suggests skulduggery, but here it is literal: a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuna is a large sea fish, so it is literally something fishy, the question mark flagging the pun.

clue.text: Worldwide student poetry almost entirely unfinished

parts.note: uni, short for university, is where the student is, the setter's stand-in for student

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the poetry word is dropped

parts.note: verse means poetry

indicators.note: unfinished means the word for entirely loses its final letter

parts.note: all means entirely

explanation.surface: Global student verse is nearly all incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims VERSE to VERS and 'unfinished' trims ALL to AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Universal means applying everywhere, across the whole world.

clue.text: Protection say accepted by road workers ultimately

indicators.note: the road and the last letter take in the example, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: the A1 is Britain's longest road, written AI in crosswords
eg, for example, is what say means

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of workers

explanation.surface: Safety for instance taken on by the people mending the highway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'road workers' looks like one unit but splits: the A1 road and the end of 'workers'.
explanation.definitionFit: Aegis means protection or sponsorship, from the shield of Zeus in Greek myth.

clue.text: Nothing from speaker left tucking into two molluscs

indicators.note: a speaker says the word aloud, so we want letters that sound like it

parts.note: naught is an old word for nothing

indicators.note: left is tucked inside two, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: II is two in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone eats a pair of shellfish and leaves nothing behind.
explanation.walkthrough: NAUT spoken is the same as naught, nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautili are sea creatures with spiral chambered shells, cephalopod molluscs related to squid.

clue.text: Suspicion of fluid ejected by octopuses and marine fish?

parts.note: octopuses squirt ink to escape predators
the ling is a long sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A query about what squirts from octopuses and some sea fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that a ling does not eject ink; the clue is read in two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: An inkling is a faint notion or slight suspicion that something is so.

clue.text: Be generally hospitable, eager to welcome religious leader home

indicators.note: eager welcomes the religious leader inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: keen means eager
the Pope leads the Roman Catholic Church
a house is a home

explanation.surface: Keen to receive the pontiff into one's house, a model of hospitality.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep open house is the idiom for welcoming guests at any time, being hospitable to all comers.

clue.text: Prelude of note in Italian romantic opera, originally

indicators.note: the note is placed inside the Italian romantic opera letters

parts.note: n. is the abbreviation used for a note, as in a footnote reference

indicators.note: originally points to the starting letters of romantic and opera

explanation.surface: A musical overture worth noticing in an Italian romantic opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks musical but is the reference-book N, as in n. 3; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is an introductory passage, a short opening section like a prelude.

clue.text: Dish encountered in hospital department, on Sundays principally

indicators.note: encountered goes inside the rest, the hospital department and what follows

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
RE means concerning, on the subject of

indicators.note: principally points to the opening letter of Sundays

parts.note: met means encountered

explanation.surface: A meal someone came across in a hospital ward, mostly on Sundays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the encountered piece inside everything after it, not just inside the hospital department; RE for 'on' is the crossword sense 'concerning'.
explanation.definitionFit: Entremets is a French culinary term for a side course or sweet served between main courses.

clue.text: Popular fellow playing on lute, say, right away

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
Stan is a man's name, standing for any fellow

indicators.note: playing suggests the words are performed in a fresh arrangement, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A well-liked chap plays the lute at once when asked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' shuffles ON LUTE SAY into TANEOUSLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Instantaneously means immediately, at once, without any delay.

clue.text: Absurdity of way Charlie gets thrown by greed

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way

indicators.note: greed throws Charlie off, so that letter is removed

parts.note: cupidity means greed
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: How silly it is that a man named Charlie is unseated by avarice.
explanation.definitionFit: Stupidity is foolishness, behaviour that makes no sense, as absurdity is.

clue.text: Unexpectedly godly line in vocalisation?

indicators.note: the letters fall in a surprising new order, so the words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A surprisingly holy phrase sung out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link; the question mark marks the definition as an example of a vocal style.
explanation.definitionFit: Yodelling is singing that flips between chest voice and falsetto, a distinctive Alpine kind of vocal sound.

clue.text: Raced after lookalike, such as Fink-Nottle for example

indicators.note: raced comes after lookalike, so it is placed second

parts.note: a double is someone who looks just like another
barrelled means sped along, raced

explanation.surface: A rush after a doppelganger, with a Wodehouse character as a case in point.
explanation.walkthrough: Gussie Fink-Nottle is a character in P. G. Wodehouse's Jeeves stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Fink-Nottle is a surname made of two joined names, which is what a hyphenated double-barrelled name is.

clue.text: Footsore person of second celebrity group?

definitions.text: Footsore person of second celebrity group?

parts.words: Footsore person of second celebrity group
parts.note: a minor celebrity, one on the B list, imagined as a sore spot on the foot by splitting the word after its first letter

explanation.surface: A query about a weary-footed member of the second tier of the famous.
explanation.walkthrough: The name for a second-rank celebrity, a B-lister, is also the word for a sore bubble on the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A fluid-filled bump on the skin from rubbing makes the foot sore, and a second-rank star is a B-lister.

clue.text: Joker finally in euphoric state, as the Marx Brothers were

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of Joker

parts.note: elated means euphoric

explanation.surface: A comedian at last overjoyed, like the famous comedy siblings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link here: the last letter of Joker comes before the euphoric state.
explanation.definitionFit: The Marx Brothers were siblings, members of one family, so kin to each other.

clue.text: Male, one Conservative on radio introducing a Liberal leader

parts.note: Ed is a man's name, standing for any male
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: on radio means said aloud, so letters that sound the same are wanted

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A man, a broadcasting Tory, presents a Liberal leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' is not the Liberal's chief but a newspaper's leading article; TORI spoken is the same as Tory.
explanation.definitionFit: In British newspapers a leader is the main opinion article, the paper's editorial.

clue.text: English doctor on American board

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree
US means American

explanation.surface: A British physician sits on a US committee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'board' looks like a committee but is a verb: get on a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: To embus is to get on a bus, to board a vehicle, especially of troops.

clue.text: Meat Muslims consume, primarily available in communal dining area

indicators.note: the first letter of available is put inside the dining area

parts.note: a hall, as in a college dining hall

indicators.note: primarily points to the opening letter of available

explanation.surface: Meat for Muslims is mostly on offer in a shared canteen.
explanation.definitionFit: Halal food is prepared under Islamic law, the meat permitted for Muslims to eat.

clue.text: Some fill a novel — that's plain

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of padding out a book is obvious enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's plain' reads as 'that is obvious' but is a definition: a grassy plain.
explanation.definitionFit: A llano is a broad treeless grassland of South America, a type of plain.

clue.text: Joint gamble involving danger

indicators.note: the gamble takes in the danger, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a bet is a gamble
risk means danger

explanation.surface: A shared wager that carries some peril.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' looks like an adjective, shared, but it is a cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Brisket is a cut of beef from the breast, a joint of meat for roasting.

clue.text: Wave initially to Sophie, a friend in Paris

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letters of to and Sophie

parts.note: in French, a friend is un ami

explanation.surface: A greeting gesture first made to Sophie, a French pal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wave' looks like a hand gesture of greeting but is a huge sea wave.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsunami is a giant sea wave set off by an earthquake or undersea landslide.

clue.text: Leguminous plant, one originally unknown in South Africa

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the abbreviation for South Africa
originally points to the opening letter of one

parts.note: in algebra y is an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: A bean plant, once a mystery, is found in South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Soya is a bean plant, a legume grown for its protein-rich seeds.

clue.text: Noted creation for sending off new issue?

definitions.text: Noted creation for sending off new issue?

parts.words: Noted creation for sending off new issue
parts.note: a piece of music written to send a newborn child to sleep

explanation.surface: A query about something produced to dispatch a new edition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noted' means set to musical notes, 'new issue' is a baby, and 'sending off' is sending to sleep, not dispatching a publication.
explanation.definitionFit: A lullaby is a song sung to soothe a baby to sleep in its crib.
